chunks: From him, from Ibrahim, from al-Barqi, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from Musa ibn Hamzah ibn Bazee', who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, I have an estate near Baghdad, so I leave Kufa intending Baghdad, and I will stay in that estate; should I shorten the prayer or complete it?' He said: 'If you do not intend to stay for ten days, then shorten [the prayer].'

And the second aspect is that the narrations should be understood as referring to one who passes by a house he had previously inhabited for six months or more, in which case completing the prayer is obligatory upon him. That is indicated by what has been narrated:
ai.seo_question: When should a traveler shorten their prayers versus completing them according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the threshold for changing prayer status from travel to residence, establishing the 'ten-day' rule based on the traveler's intention. The secondary opinion highlights the concept of 'habitation' (istwatn), where a place previously lived in for six months or more reverts the individual to a resident status, requiring full prayers even during transit. This distinction is crucial in Shia fiqh for determining when the concessions of safar (travel) cease to apply.
